Practical automation

Automation should solve a recurring problem. If a simple checklist works better, use the checklist.

5 lessonsStep-by-step tutorialNo account needed

THE FIELD GUIDE / 07

Practical automationBIZZINTEL · KEEP BUILDING
How to use this guide

Read one lesson, complete the action in your business, and keep the result somewhere you can find it. The examples are illustrations, not claims about real customers.

LESSON 01 / 05

Find repetitive work

You should automate a measurable problem.

What to do

  1. List tasks, frequency, owner, errors, cost and what would happen if a system failed.
  2. Record the result in your workbook.
  3. Verify important details before treating the task as finished.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

Copying generic advice without checking that it fits your market, customer and costs.

↗
What you should finish with

Ranked automation opportunity list.

Evidence to capture: Your written output or link to the relevant source
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Give me an automation audit worksheet for my business. Rank repetitive tasks by frequency, time saved, failure risk and implementation complexity.
LESSON 02 / 05

Draw the workflow

Undefined processes make fragile automations.

What to do

  1. Map trigger, inputs, owner, action and exceptions.
  2. Try a normal rule before using AI.
  3. Define exact point for human approval.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

AVOID THIS

LESSON 03 / 05

Choose a sensible tool

Complex tools are not always necessary.

What to do

  1. Compare existing software features, basic rules, n8n, Zapier and AI assistance only when the task calls for it.
  2. Record the result in your workbook.
  3. Verify important details before treating the task as finished.

LESSON 04 / 05

Test edge cases

Automations break outside perfect demos.

What to do

  1. Test invalid input, duplicate events and timeouts.
  2. Confirm credentials never appear in public tools.
  3. Add a safe fallback and escalation to a person.

LESSON 05 / 05

Launch with control

Operational mistakes are expensive.

What to do

  1. Start with a small group, record errors, document how to turn it off and measure the improvement.
  2. Record the result in your workbook.
  3. Verify important details before treating the task as finished.
